summary.text: A 17-year-old girl with SLE nephritis, followed for 8 years and with first manifestations of ecchymosis and gingival bleeding after tooth extraction at 9 years of age, had positive lupus anticoagulant and antiphospholipid antibodies with intermittently prolonged PT and aPTT but no severe bleeding or thrombosis. She presented with colicky abdominal pain for a day.

Examination found generalized abdominal tenderness, hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL, platelets 74,000/uL, PT 18.3 seconds, aPTT 68.9 seconds and a positive lupus anticoagulant. Imaging showed a hemorrhagic right ovarian cyst. Close observation was advised, MMF was reduced, steroid increased and tacrolimus added for suspected SLE flaring.

Three months later she had dizziness, persistent menorrhagia and hemoglobin 7.4 g/dL, requiring red blood cell transfusion and a combined oral contraceptive pill. Persistently prolonged aPTT, low factor II and PT and aPTT that stayed prolonged on mixing were reported, LAHPS associated with SLE was diagnosed, and MMF and tacrolimus were increased. Epistaxis, menorrhagia and worsening proteinuria followed, with a second biopsy showing class III A/C lupus nephritis; she was re-admitted for plasma transfusion and six courses of intravenous cyclophosphamide.

Her general condition is improving with decreased proteinuria (UPCR 0.35), although prolonged PT and aPTT, low factor II and positive lupus anticoagulant persisted without bleeding or thrombotic complications. She currently takes cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, enalapril and a steroid, and low-dose aspirin cannot be used at present.

ambiguities.issue: The Figure 1 caption describes the abdominal ultrasound finding as a 4.9 x 4.1 x 5 cm heterogeneous mass in the uterus, while the case text describes the ultrasound and CT finding as a 4.7 cm hemorrhagic right ovarian cyst.

evidence.quote: (A) A 4.9×4.1×5 cm heterogeneous mass (arrow) in the uterus on abdominal ultrasonography
Abdominal ultrasonography and pelvic computed tomography revealed a 4.7 cm-sized hemorrhagic right ovarian cyst

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which organ or size is correct, merge the two ultrasound findings, or assign the 4.7 cm size to the CT alone.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says the hemorrhagic ovarian cyst resolved completely in 3 months, while the case text and Figure 1C describe a decreasing-sized or reduced lesion (<2 cm) at the same three-month point; the caption calls the study abdominal ultrasonography, the text pelvic ultrasonography. Both sides agree the lesion shrank; whether it persisted is in conflict.

article_limitations: Case report of one patient; literature statements about LAHPS cohorts and mechanisms are background, not patient facts.
Figure 1A caption and the case text disagree on the ultrasound site and size; the abstract says the cyst resolved completely in 3 months while the text and caption describe a reduced lesion.
The case text names deflazacort and the discussion names prednisolone as the current steroid.
Most events lack calendar dates; Three months later, Since then and 5 days later are anchored only to the adjacent sentences.
Values printed inside the Figure 3 chart are pixel content for the visual record only and are not facts here.
